title: Token-churn aware segmentation and fragmentation healing for KV cache
creator: Amira Chen
description:
Problem: Long-lived KV entries from conversational workloads cause fragmentation and uneven occupancy in GPU-resident KV pools. Continuous batching increases the variance in live-set lifetimes because very long horizon requests (chat) coexist with many short requests (single-turn completion). This ticket designs and implements a token-churn aware allocation strategy plus a low-latency fragmentation healing path to reclaim space without introducing significant tail latency or violating KV cache correctness.

Scope: 1) Runtime allocator changes to support occupancy bucketing (hot/warm/cold) keyed by token churn estimates, 2) lightweight in-place slot compaction for low-fragmentation windows, 3) background epochal rewriting for high-fragmentation pools with scheduling that respects latency SLO and batching behavior, 4) telemetry and safety gates (rate limits, fallback to eviction-first) and 5) integration tests and benchmarks on representative multi-tenant traces.

Non-goals: Full offline defragmenter that pauses serving; large-scale cross-GPU shuffling; model-level parameter edits. Those are out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: New allocation path classifies allocations by churn using per-token lifetime estimator and places entries into hot/warm/cold subpools
End-to-end throughput for continuous-batching workloads does not regress by more than 3% under P95 latency SLO compared to baseline
Fragmentation (measured as unusable free bytes ratio) reduced by >= 40% for heavy-churn synthetic trace after a single healing pass
Background healing tasks never increase P99 generation latency by more than 5ms under standard traffic mix
Automated integration test reproduces churn pattern and validates correctness (no KV corruption) and recovery path
Design doc, PR, and runtime benchmark results posted to Confluence and GitHub with reproducible scripts
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Serving, and Observability teams. Agreed to use a hybrid approach: fast-path in-place relocation for small gaps + epochal rewrite for high-fragment areas.

2026-02-22: Prototype allocator added: per-shard occupancy histograms and churn estimator based on recent token lifetimes. Initial microbench shows slightly higher allocation CPU (≈5%) but lower fragmentation on synthetic churn trace.
2026-03-01: Design review with PM (Riley Patel) and SRE. PM requested explicit fallbacks for Dedicated customers during scheduled healing windows. SRE asked for throttles and circuit-breaker metrics.

2026-03-04: Implemented fast-path in-place relocation that moves KV slots within same memory region to coalesce free ranges. Benchmark: healing pass reduced unusable bytes by 28% with median CPU overhead of 2%. Caused a 3ms tail latency bump under microburst—added rate limiting.

2026-03-07: Integrated with continuous batching by tagging batch requests with 'batch-lease' so healing avoids relocating KV entries pinned by active batches. This eliminated correctness hazards where in-flight KV pointers could be invalidated.

2026-03-09: Submitted PR for allocator changes and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4301. Note: CI flaky on deterministic eviction test—investigating ordering non-determinism under stress fixtures.

2026-03-10: Performance run on p4d cluster: observed 45% fragmentation reduction after a full epochal rewrite on heavy churn trace; P95 latency within target. Preparing release notes and rollout plan for runtime-1.20 canary.
